project.title: PNIPAM Lattice Model: Experiment-to-Simulation Validation and Aggregation Roadmap
project.purpose: Develop and validate a transferable lattice model of PNIPAM that connects atomistic REMD simulations, experimental radius-of-gyration measurements, thermal transition curves, polymer scaling, and multi-chain aggregation.
project.central_question: Can a local temperature-dependent lattice contact free energy fitted to short PNIPAM chains predict longer-chain conformational and collective behavior without chain-length-specific refitting?

current_reference_state.main_known_issue: Athermal support mismatch, especially at high temperature and increasingly with chain length.
current_reference_state.current_rg_interpretation: The lattice model is not uniformly smaller than the molecular model. It is slightly lower at some temperatures and slightly higher at others. The remaining mean-Rg bias is small, but the fitted rg_scale is not yet an independent prediction.

potentially_transferable: Temperature-dependent local contact free energy b(T)
Lattice geometry, if coarse-graining remains physically appropriate
One physical lattice spacing, if validated across chain length
Local stiffness parameter, if calibrated independently from low-temperature molecular data
not_directly_transferable: The contact offset as a universal physical contact count
The fitted rg_scale unless shown to be chain-length independent
transferability_principles.key_rule: Transfer the interaction law, not the sampled 44-mer ensemble.

phase_1_short_chain_transferability.objective: Test whether the fitted contact free energy and Rg scale transfer between N=30 and N=44.
tasks: Freeze the current model parameters, contact definitions, and rg_scale.
Fit on N=44 and predict N=30 without refitting.
Fit on N=30 and predict N=44 without refitting.
Fit one shared b(T) to both chains.
Fit chain-specific rg scales only as diagnostics.
Compare mean Rg, full P(Rg|T), mean contacts, P(m|T), JS divergence, RMSE, transition midpoint, and transition width.
validation_gate: One b(T) predicts both chains with acceptable error, or
Any failure is localized to Rg mapping, stiffness, end effects, or contact mapping.

phase_2_chain_length_generalization.objective: Make the codebase work for arbitrary chain length without hard-coded assumptions.
tasks: Create a general project configuration schema.
Refactor baseline generation and REMD scripts for arbitrary N.
Standardize outputs, metadata, checkpoints, and resume behavior.
Add unit tests for contacts, Rg, self-avoidance, replica exchange, and periodic unwrapping.

phase_3_n_series.objective: Test chain-length scaling and transition behavior.

sampling_strategy.N_le_120: Use high-statistics athermal baselines when support diagnostics pass.
sampling_strategy.N_ge_200: Prefer direct REMD or density-of-states methods such as multicanonical or Wang-Landau sampling.

phase_4_polymer_scaling.objective: Determine whether one interaction law reproduces PNIPAM size scaling.
analysis: Fit A(T) and nu(T) at every temperature.
Analyze transition width, peak susceptibility, and heat-capacity scaling.

phase_5_direct_experiment_connection.objective: Compare experiment, molecular REMD, and lattice simulations using one fixed physical mapping.
experimental_metadata_required: Whether the reported size is single-chain or collective
phase_5_direct_experiment_connection.length_scale_strategy: Determine one lattice spacing from low-temperature multi-N data, then freeze it for all other temperatures.
comparison_levels: Normalized experimental Rg(T) versus normalized lattice Rg(T)

synthetic_scattering.molecular: Compute atom-weighted and monomer-center scattering with experimental contrast where possible.
synthetic_scattering.analysis_rule: Use the same q-range and fit model as the experiment.

phase_6_thermal_transition_curves.objective: Compare structural collapse and calorimetric transition behavior.

model_roles.hs_quadratic: More flexible descriptive model that may absorb missing physics.

decision_tree.correct_transition_wrong_RgN: Add or calibrate chain stiffness and revisit lattice length mapping.
decision_tree.Rg_agrees_heat_capacity_fails: Improve thermodynamics or introduce explicit hydration states.
decision_tree.single_chain_agrees_cloud_point_fails: Proceed to a multi-chain model rather than refitting the single-chain model.
decision_tree.sampling_support_fails: Use direct REMD or density-of-states methods.

possible_extensions: Bending penalty calibrated from molecular tangent correlations
phase_7_missing_physics_diagnostics.model_selection_rule: Accept added complexity only if it improves held-out chain lengths or temperatures, not only the training fit.

phase_8_multichain_aggregation.objective: Test whether the single-chain interaction predicts aggregation without refitting.

minimal_model.system: M connected self-avoiding chains of length N in a periodic box

observables.m_intra: Nonbonded contacts within the same chain

phase_9_finite_size_and_phase_behavior.objective: Distinguish equilibrium mesoglobules, metastable clusters, and finite-size representations of macroscopic phase separation.
phase_9_finite_size_and_phase_behavior.protocol: Increase M and box size L together at fixed chain length, concentration, and interaction parameters.

interpretation.macroscopic_phase_separation: Largest cluster grows with system size and coarsening continues.
interpretation.equilibrium_mesoglobules: Finite aggregate size converges with increasing total system size.
interpretation.metastable_clusters: Apparent size depends strongly on time or initialization and continues to evolve.

immediate_next_sprint.goal: Determine whether the current interaction law and Rg scale transfer between N=30 and N=44.
tasks: Create frozen reference manifests for N=30 and N=44.
Reproduce all current metrics.
Implement analyze_rg_transferability.py.
Implement run_cross_chain_prediction.py.
Implement transition_curve_metrics.py.
Run 44-to-30 and 30-to-44 no-refit predictions.
Run one joint fit.
Compare fixed and diagnostic Rg scales.
Generate residual, distribution, and transition plots.
Write a go/no-go report for the N-series.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-chain predictions run without manual code changes.
Fixed and diagnostic Rg scales are reported.
Any failure is localized to a specific part of the mapping.
The next scientific decision is supported quantitatively.

long_term: Map aggregation versus temperature and concentration.

minimum: Chain-length scaling through at least N=200
strong: One b(T) and one lattice spacing describe molecular and experimental size data
Transition curves agree without chain-specific refitting
complete: The same local interaction predicts single-chain collapse and multi-chain aggregation
Any added terms are physically interpretable and improve held-out predictions
Finite-size scaling distinguishes phase separation from stable finite aggregates
